name: From Latent Knowledge to Reliable Answers

papers.title: Blinded by Generated Contexts: How Language Models Merge Generated and Retrieved Contexts When Knowledge Conflicts?
papers.venue_full: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
papers.summary: Controlled knowledge-conflict experiments reveal a preference for generated over retrieved context, including incorrect generated passages, and examine the roles of question similarity and semantic completeness.

papers.title: Too Consistent to Detect: A Study of Self-Consistent Errors in LLMs
papers.venue_full: Proceedings of the 2025 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
papers.summary: Defines self-consistent errors, evaluates their prevalence and the limitations of four error-detection approaches, and introduces a supervised cross-model probe using verifier hidden states.

papers.title: Beyond Reasoning: Reinforcement Learning Unlocks Parametric Knowledge in LLMs
papers.summary: Studies correctness-reward reinforcement learning for one-hop closed-book factual recall without explicit chain-of-thought, finding evidence that RL improves access to suppressed correct answers.

papers.title: When to Trust LLMs: Aligning Confidence with Response Quality
papers.venue_full: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2024
papers.summary: CONQORD combines quality and order-preserving alignment rewards to align verbalized confidence with response quality, with an application to deciding when retrieval augmentation may help.

papers.title: BaseCal: Unsupervised Confidence Calibration via Base Model Signals
papers.venue_full: Proceedings of the 64th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
papers.summary: Uses a corresponding base model as a reference for post-trained confidence, through answer reevaluation or an unsupervised representation projection, while retaining the original answering model.

papers.title: Fact-Level Calibration and Correction for Long-Form Generations
papers.venue_full: Proceedings of the 48th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval
papers.version: SIGIR 2025 published version; author preprint has an earlier title and method name
papers.summary: Studies calibration at the level of atomic facts, incorporating correctness and relevance, and introduces CARE to use high-confidence facts to help refine lower-confidence claims in long responses.

papers.title: Resisting Contextual Interference in RAG via Parametric-Knowledge Reinforcement
papers.summary: Knowledgeable-R1 uses paired retrieval-free and retrieval-conditioned training signals to reinforce parametric knowledge and improve robustness to misleading context while using helpful external evidence.

papers.title: Strong yet Controllable LLM Abstention without Learning to Abstain
papers.summary: TAPS separates accuracy training from confidence-based answer selection, examining answering and distinguishing abilities at matched coverage while keeping the answer rate adjustable.
